stations.title: Founded by Bishop Bernhard
stations.text: Bishop Bernhard of Prambach founded a Cistercian monastery in 1293; in 1295 it was settled by monks from its mother house, Wilhering.

stations.title: Dissolved by Emperor Joseph II
stations.text: Emperor Joseph II dissolved the monastery in 1786 as part of his monastic reforms. Afterward the buildings served, among other things, as a factory and a residence.

stations.title: Departure from Switzerland
stations.text: French troops invaded Switzerland. Augustin de Lestrange set out with more than 200 monks, nuns and children from the Carthusian monastery of Val-Sainte near Fribourg—the beginning of a two-year flight across Europe.

stations.title: A resting place at Engelszell
stations.text: In 1798 the empty buildings of the abbey, dissolved in 1786, unexpectedly served monastic life once more: 254 Trappist monks, nuns and children rested here on their way through Germany, Austria, Bohemia and Poland, traveling further east.

stations.title: Settling in Volhynia
stations.text: Tsar Paul I allowed the community to settle in the monastery of Zydyczyn (Volhynia, now Ukraine). The first winter, at around −30 °C, proved almost unbearable. In March 1800 the Tsar ordered all French émigrés to be expelled; at Easter that year, on April 13, the Trappists had to leave Russia as well.

stations.title: Back across the Baltic
stations.text: Expelled from Russia, the community traveled across the Baltic Sea to Lübeck. In 1801/1802 those returning from Russia met up again with the other scattered Trappists; in 1814, after Napoleon's defeat, La Trappe itself could finally be resettled.

stations.title: Refounded by exiled monks
stations.text: German monks, expelled after the First World War from Oelenberg Abbey in Alsace, first found refuge in Banz Abbey and in 1925 refounded Engelszell—this time as a Trappist monastery. In 1931 the priory was raised to an abbey, with Gregorius Eisvogel as its first abbot.

stations.title: Expelled by the Gestapo
stations.text: The Gestapo seized the abbey on December 2, 1939 and expelled the community of 73. Four monks were sent to Dachau concentration camp; others were imprisoned or conscripted into the Wehrmacht.

stations.title: Return after the war
stations.text: About a third of the community returned in 1945, reinforced by German Trappists who had been expelled from Mariastern Abbey in Banja Luka (now in Bosnia).

stations.title: The ninth Trappist brewery
stations.text: With only seven monks left in the community, the International Trappist Association recognized Engelszell in May 2012 as the ninth Trappist brewery—only the second outside Belgium.

stations.title: The end of the community
stations.text: The Order dissolved the community on May 15, 2023. The last four remaining monks declared that they could no longer sustain a Trappist life in the monastery. The brewery continues under new, lay management—without the Trappist seal.
